evals.prompt: Using the supplied map-contract.md source packet, create a compact Mermaid figure explaining Operators.Map.map_commutes for a research note. Include a caption describing the relationship and its domain, with a source citation. Save diagram.mmd and figure.md locally. Use only the supplied sources.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads local constraints and the actual declaration, preserves WellRankedSeq rank ts and all ranks including zero, compares decode rank (map f (encode rank ts)) with ts.map (Tensor.map f), and grounds the caption in map_commutes. It does not turn a simulator run into a universal proof. It supplies Mermaid and a caption, and distinguishes rendering from source inspection and destination verification.
assertions: The diagram and caption compare decode rank (map f (encode rank ts)) with ts.map (Tensor.map f), without asserting a stronger equality.
The caption preserves the premise WellRankedSeq rank ts.
The domain permits every natural-number rank, including zero; no positive-rank restriction is invented.
The figure cites the supplied map_commutes declaration and preserves the function and rank parameters.
The Mermaid source and caption agree on node meaning and edge direction.
The delivered SVG and PNG artifacts are valid outputs consistent with the source.
Light/dark figures are readable without clipping or misleading layout at the supplied display size.

evals.prompt: Using the supplied systems-protocol.md, create a compact Mermaid experiment-protocol figure for a computer-systems paper. Show the baseline/candidate comparison and the controls, measurement stages, and failure accounting. Include a caption, save diagram.mmd and figure.md, and show the local rendered preview. Use only the supplied protocol.
evals.expected_output: A controlled systems benchmark diagram with matched workloads and environment, distinct correctness checking/warm-up/timing, and visible failure accounting. The caption preserves five warm-ups, twenty measured invocations, kernel-only timing, and no implied concurrent execution or invented speedup.
assertions: Baseline and candidate share the supplied input values, workload matrix, host, compiler, and thread count.
The reference correctness check precedes timing; incorrect configurations are reported and not timed.
Five warm-ups are untimed; twenty invocation timings exclude allocation and input generation.
Failed and timed-out trials remain reported; missing comparisons are not turned into speedup claims.
The diagram does not assert concurrent execution, a randomized run order, or any measured results.
Source, caption, and rendered previews agree on directions, conditions, and line-style meanings.
Actual previews at the stated document width have readable labels and no overlaps or clipped arrows.

evals.prompt: Using the supplied branching-kernel.md, draw a Mermaid control-flow figure for the tiled kernel. Preserve the empty-input case, fast-path guard, safe fallback, reconvergence, valid stores, and tile loop. Use a 720 CSS-pixel documentation preview in light and dark themes. Save diagram.mmd and figure.md with a caption and show the actual previews. Use only the supplied algorithm.
evals.expected_output: A readable branching-and-looping kernel figure whose main progression, mutually exclusive paths, merge, and loop exit remain visible at the delivery width. All scientific claims come from the synthetic source, with no added parallelism or barriers.
assertions: The n=0 path returns before loads, computation, or stores.
The vector path requires both a full tile and alignment; the fallback covers their complement.
The mutually exclusive paths rejoin at the shared elementwise transform, not an invented parallel barrier.
Stores affect valid elements only, and iteration returns to selecting the next tile until completion.
The caption preserves n≥0 and B>0 and declares control-flow arrow semantics.
Rendered decision labels, loop edge, merges, and exit remain distinguishable without clipping or overlaps in both themes at 720 CSS pixels.

evals.prompt: Using architecture-change.md, create a Mermaid research figure explaining how explicit dependencies enable selective recomputation compared with the supplied fixed pipeline. Include a source-grounded caption. Save diagram.mmd and figure.md and render light/dark previews at 720 CSS pixels. Use only the supplied source.
evals.expected_output: Corresponding mechanisms with visible change-impact resolution, retained unaffected results, and index updates; qualified capability, no invented measured gains.
assertions: Both architectures maintain results after a source-data change; the supplied baseline reruns all stages unconditionally, while the proposed system selects affected results, possibly all results.
The dependency index informs affected-result selection; the scheduler recomputes affected results in dependency order.
Unaffected cached results are retained and combined with recomputed results; recomputation updates the index for later events.
The caption preserves complete dependency recording and change detection assumptions; no speedup or universal baseline limitation is invented.
The changed mechanism and capability are identifiable at 720 CSS pixels in both themes; source, caption, and accessible description agree.

evals.prompt: Using iterative-repair.md, create a Mermaid figure explaining how counterexamples guide candidate repair across rounds. Preserve what remains fixed, what accumulates, and the meaning of every termination outcome. Save diagram.mmd and figure.md with a caption and render light/dark previews at 720 CSS pixels.
evals.expected_output: Fixed specification and domain, retained counterexamples, candidate revision and recheck, and distinct verified/unknown/repair-exhausted outcomes without invented total termination.
assertions: Initialization occurs once; the fixed specification and allowed domain constrain checking and repair.
Verified, counterexample, and unknown are distinct checker outcomes; unknown is inconclusive.
Each counterexample is added to the retained set; repair uses the current candidate, specification, and entire accumulated set.
A revised candidate returns to checking, not initialization; repair exhaustion is not proof of impossibility and known-example satisfaction is not verification.
The diagram and caption preserve the per-round search budget without inventing overall termination; labels and return paths remain readable at 720 CSS pixels.

evals.prompt: Using feedback-loops.md, draw a Mermaid mechanism figure explaining how design optimization and predictor calibration affect one another. Preserve their actual information exchanges and triggers. Save diagram.mmd and figure.md with a caption and render light/dark previews at 720 CSS pixels.
evals.expected_output: Two distinct updated objects linked by archived observations and revised estimates; direct measurement feedback, fixed feasibility constraint, event-driven calibration, no invented nested schedule or convergence.
assertions: The proposer uses predictor estimates and prior measured performance under the fixed feasibility specification.
Evaluation archives design/measurement pairs and feeds measured performance back to subsequent proposals.
Prediction error compares archived predictions with measurements; it is not equated with measured performance.
Unacceptable prediction error triggers archive-based calibration; the updated predictor informs future design proposals.
No fixed calibration frequency, strict loop nesting, terminal condition, barrier, measured improvement, or convergence claim is invented.
The two mutable objects and cross-loop payloads are identifiable without relying on color alone at the delivery width.

evals.prompt: Using context-and-constraints.md, create a Mermaid assay-methods figure explaining the specimen path and how supporting information affects it. evals.expected_output: Visible specimen progression, SOP constraint, literature-informed model selection, calibration input, and drift-triggered recalibration without serializing context or inventing reprocessing.
assertions: The specimen path retains preparation, acquisition, concentration estimation, and reporting in the supplied order.
The SOP constrains preparation; literature informs model selection and the selected model enters estimation.
Known-reference measurements fit calibration coefficients before the batch; coefficients enter estimation.
Quality-control acquisition supplies observed drift, with unacceptable drift triggering recalibration for subsequent estimates.
No retroactive correction, batch reprocessing, automatic rejection, randomization, or measured result is invented.
Background, constraints, processed inputs, and feedback are distinguishable without losing their specific targets; source and caption agree with the visible paths.
